title: stability-action-notebook-ops-experiment-roster-45
content:
Purpose
Quick experimental playbook + 45-day runway for reliability program adoption across serving, platform, and product teams. This is a working notebook: notes, hypotheses, run lists, staffing, and shallow runbooks for quick unblock. Not a finished charter.

Context
- Redwood is pushing SLO adoption for model-serving surfaces (hosted API + dedicated) in Q2. Need low-friction experiments that produce signal (latency/cost/quality) and produce repeatable playbooks.
- Focus: make small, measurable changes teams can own (cache knobs, batching windows, routing fallbacks).

Goals (measurable)
- Establish 3 cross-team experiments that each produce at least one actionable insight by day 30.
- Reduce P99 tail latency for small-request workload by >=15% in participating services (baseline = current 99th).
- Create an error-budget policy template and get sign-off from 2 product owners.

Success metrics (primary)
- P95/P99 token-latency change (baseline vs experiment window) — per-route and aggregated.
- Error budget burn rate delta per week.
- Percent of requests served from KV/prefix cache (delta).
- CPU/GPU utilization delta and cost-per-1k-tokens estimate.
- Rollout readiness score (checklist completion) for canary > 80%.

Experiment slate (week-by-week quick list)
1) Micro-batching window tuning (serving-runtime) — 7–10 days
   Hypothesis: Increasing max batch wait from 3ms to 6ms yields net cost savings with <=5% added median latency.
   Measurement: per-batch token/time, median latency, P99, cost estimate. Canary on non-critical routes.
   Quick runbook: small config, 10% traffic, monitor tail.

2) KV cache prefix warmup + synthetic priming (platform+runtime) — 10–14 days
   Hypothesis: Proactively priming KV cache for top-10 prefixes reduces cold-start P99 by 30%.
   Measurement: cache-hit %, cold-start count, P99 for first-request sequences.
   Notes: use synthetic warmup job that simulates top prompt prefixes during low-traffic windows.

3) Latency-aware routing fallback (smart routing) — 14 days
   Hypothesis: Route to a slightly lower-capacity but lower-queued model variant for 20% of requests during spikes will keep overall P99 within SLO while maintaining throughput.
   Measurement: request success, P99, throughput, cost per token.
   Risk: potential quality regressions — attach quick A/B sample to verify scoring.

4) Error-budget micro-policy + automated pause (ops) — 7 days
   Hypothesis: Implementing a conservative auto-pause when burn rate exceeds 2x reduces incident blast radius and stabilizes SLOs.
   Measurement: incidents prevented, time-to-recover.
   Runbook: tie to alerting and oncall playbook; manual override.

5) Small-request optimizations (client-side + runtime batching hints) — 10 days
   Hypothesis: For short sequences (<16 tokens) enabling a 'fast-path' micro-batch reduces median latency significantly.
   Measurement: median latency, client error rates.

Staffing & roles (45-day roster)
- Experiment lead (overall): Aisha Patel — coordinates cross-team, weekly syncs.
- Serving runtime engineer (micro-batching): Marcus Lee — implements canary and metrics hooks.
- Platform/infra (cache priming): Priya Nair — create priming job, storage quotas.
- Product-owner liaisons: Diego Alvarez (Hosted API), Sam O'Connor (Dedicated) — approve canaries, product impact.
- SLO analyst: temporary rotation from Reliability (3d/wk) — owns dashboards and metric health.
- Oncall coverage: SRE rotation — pre-scheduled for canary windows.

RACI (high level)
- Responsible: experiment leads and engineers listed above.
- Accountable: eng-sre manager (named in Confluence).
- Consulted: product owners, solutions eng for customer impact.
- Informed: all participating feature teams via #slo-experiments slack channel.

Signal & dashboards (minimal viable telemetry)
- Central dashboard: SLO-experiments (Grafana) with lanes: latency (P50/P95/P99), errors (class counts), cache-hits, cost-estimate.
- Synthetic probes: real-user sampling + synthetic sequences for cold starts.
- Alerts: two-tier: (1) fast alert: P99 > threshold for 10m; (2) burn alert: error-budget burn > X%/hr.

Timeline (45-day)
- Day 0–3: kickoff, finalize hypothesis, toggle plan, enable base-line dashboards.
- Day 4–14: run experiments 1 & 5 concurrently (micro-batching + fast-path).
- Day 10–24: run experiment 2 (cache priming) with limited blast radius.
- Day 18–32: run experiment 3 (routing fallback) on small slice.
- Day 25–35: error-budget policy pilot and integrate with alerts.
- Day 36–45: consolidate signals, write playbooks, exec review with product owners.

Communication plan
- Weekly 30m sync: Monday 10:00 PT (standup + blockers).
- Daily asynchronous updates: short note in #slo-experiments channel with key delta metric.
- Stakeholder review at day 15 & day 45 with executive summary.

Decision gates (must-pass to expand rollout)
- Gate A (canary pass): P99 within target OR error budget burn <= baseline*1.1 for 24h window.
- Gate B (quality check): no statistically significant regression in ranking/score/quality for sampled requests (A/B).
- Gate C (ops readiness): runbook completed, rollback tested, oncall trained.

Risk register (top items)
- Quality regressions from routing to model variants — mitigate with A/B scoring and conservative traffic %.
- Overlap of experiments creating confounding signals — mitigate with staggered windows and control groups.
- Insufficient telemetry resolution — mitigate by adding high-cardinality probes for suspect routes.
- Cost increase from mis-tuned batching — budget cap and auto-revert thresholds.

Playbooks to produce (deliverables)
- Lightweight SLO adoption template for feature teams (1 pager).
- Canaries checklist and rollback script (ops-runbook).
- Experiment report template (what we measured, what we changed, recommendation).
- Error-budget micro-policy with automated pause logic.

Action items (first 7 days)
- [Aisha] finalize experiment definitions and publish kickoff doc (this doc).
- [Marcus] implement canary config for micro-batching, add metrics hook.
- [Priya] prototype KV priming job and storage schedule.
- [Diego+Sam] identify two non-customer-critical routes for canaries.
- [SLO analyst] baseline dashboards created and shared.
- [All] join Slack channel #slo-experiments and subscribe.

Open questions / notes to self
- Need a simple conversion from per-batch metrics to cost-per-1k-tokens that product can digest. (TODO: ask finance for cost model.)
- How to interpret quality regressions for multimodal outputs? start with text-only for these pilots.
- Can we leverage existing Redwood Optimize suggestions to auto-propose batch windows? investigate.

Appendix: quick metric definitions
- P99 token-latency: end-to-end latency for last token of request.
- Cold-start: a request with zero prior KV/prefix cache hits for that exact prefix.
- Error-budget burn rate: % of allowed errors consumed per hour relative to SLO window.

References & links (working)
- Confluence: reliability playbook draft (linked_artifacts above).
- Jira epic: REL-1234 — SLO experiments runway.
- GitHub: infra repo for canary scripts.

-- end of notebook --
